source: Training/processed/taxonomy_v29.json + label_sets.json (2026-10-25). Repo-format export written by Claude (Cowork). Descriptions carried from the earlier repo v29 where the name survives.

L1.name: Progress Note
L1.description: A clinician's record of an encounter. L2 here is the CONTENT SECTION the page carries, not the kind of note, because a scanned page of a note is a page and what matters is what is on it. A note is a Progress Note whatever service produced it; the service line goes on the specialty axis.

L1.name: Lab Report
L1.description: The result of a test, study or examination performed on the patient. The distinction from Operative Note is that a result reports on looking, measuring or analysing, while an Operative Note records an intervention.

L1.name: Operative Note
L1.description: The record of an operation or an episode of intensive care: what was done in theatre, by whom, and under what anaesthesia. Repeated treatments and office procedures are Procedure Note instead.

L1.name: Procedure Note
L1.description: A treatment RECORD: a repeated therapeutic session or an administration of something to the patient. Neither an operation, which is Operative Note, nor an encounter narrative, which is Progress Note. Dialysis is the clearest case: a run is a procedure performed on a schedule and logged on a flow sheet, not a visit written up.

L1.name: Discharge Summary
L1.description: The closing documentation of an inpatient or observation stay, including its instructions, medications and transfers of care. The client treats this whole group as its own codeability bucket rather than as codeable or non-codeable.

L1.name: Clinical Summary
L1.description: A document that summarises care across a visit or many visits: CCD / Summary of Care / Transition of Care (C-CDA), After-Visit Summary, EHR patient-summary or chart-snapshot printouts. Decided by the document title.

L1.name: Demographics
L1.description: Patient identity, contact and coverage information, carrying no clinical content.

L1.name: Immunization
L1.description: A record of vaccines administered or due.

L1.name: Medication Record
L1.description: A list or administration record of what the patient is taking or has been given, including blood products.

L1.name: Order and Requisition
L1.description: An instruction to perform something: a test, a treatment, a referral. The order is not the result, which is why these never sit under Lab Report/Result.

L1.name: Problem List
L1.description: A standing list of the patient's active or historical problems. Flat by design: the page type is the whole answer and no L2 adds anything.
L1.codeability_tag: Context dependent (stand-alone vs in a note)
L1.notes: Codeable when bound into a progress note, non-codeable standing alone. Decided after the continuity step.

L1.name: Forms and Questionnaires
L1.description: A structured form completed by or about the patient. Codeability depends on context: bound into a progress note it is part of that note, standing alone it is not.

L1.name: Provider Letter
L1.description: A letter between providers or to the practice about the patient: referral letters, consultation letters, records requests (defined by purpose: any letter, fax or EHR note requesting records).

L1.name: Patient Communication
L1.description: Correspondence between the practice and the patient or another provider, and material sent to the patient.

L1.name: Administrative
L1.description: Pages that exist for the running of the practice rather than the care of the patient: scheduling, billing, coding, records management.

L1.name: Others
L1.description: A page nothing else claims. This is a routing decision, not a classification: the page goes to an auditor rather than being forced into a bucket or dropped.
L1.notes: Unrecognised page. Routed to an auditor rather than dropped.

Progress Note.name: CC/HPI
Progress Note.description: The chief complaint and the history of present illness: why the patient came and the narrative of the problem. Usually the opening page of a note.

Progress Note.name: Visit Diagnosis
Progress Note.description: The diagnosis or assessment arrived at for this encounter. Outranks every other section on a page, because a page that states the diagnosis is about the visit even if most of it is a data table.

Progress Note.name: Assessment and Plan
Progress Note.description: The clinician's reasoning and what they intend to do next. Distinguished from Visit Diagnosis by being forward-looking rather than a statement of findings.

Progress Note.name: Summary
Progress Note.description: A narrative recap of the encounter or stay, including hospital course where it appears inside a note.

Progress Note.name: Problem List
Progress Note.description: A problem list printed as a section inside a note, as opposed to a standalone problem list page, which is its own L1.

Progress Note.name: Medication List
Progress Note.description: Medications and allergies as a section inside a note. A standalone medication page is Medication Record instead.

Progress Note.name: Lab and Imaging Results
Progress Note.description: A split page of a note that carries results AND note content (history, exam, plan). A page that is wholly results is Lab Report, not this (page-essence rule).

Progress Note.name: Procedure List
Progress Note.description: A procedure described inside a note, typically done in the office. A formal operative report is Operative Note.

Progress Note.name: Vitals
Progress Note.description: A note page dominated by vital signs.

Progress Note.name: Physical Exam
Progress Note.description: Examination findings, review of systems and vital signs.

Progress Note.name: Questionnaire
Progress Note.description: A form or questionnaire bound into a note, which makes it part of that note. The same form standing alone is Forms and Questionnaires.

Progress Note.name: Patient Instructions
Progress Note.description: What the patient was told to do, and follow-up arrangements.

Progress Note.name: Signature
Progress Note.description: A page carrying the attestation and little else, typically the closing page of a note. The same evidence is the End-of-document signal used to group pages into documents.

Progress Note.name: Others
Progress Note.description: A progress note page whose section could not be determined. Most often a continuation page of body text with no header on it.

Lab Report.name: Lab Result
Lab Report.description: Specimen-based testing: chemistry, haematology, microbiology, urinalysis, genetics, coagulation.

Lab Report.name: Radiology Report
Lab Report.description: Imaging reports: plain film, CT, MRI, ultrasound, mammography, nuclear medicine, bone density. Angiography is held separately from plain CT and MR because it is a different protocol and a different code.

Lab Report.name: Pathology Report
Lab Report.description: Tissue and cell examination: biopsy, cytology, flow cytometry, molecular diagnostics.

Lab Report.name: Diagnostic Study
Lab Report.description: Any other study that produces a report: cardiac, neurological, pulmonary, sleep, vascular, endoscopic and ophthalmic. Deliberately broad. It holds many service lines at once, which is why no single specialty is implied at this level and the specialty is read from the page instead.

Operative Note.name: Surgery Report
Operative Note.description: The operative report itself: the account of an operation, its findings and its closure.

Operative Note.name: Procedure List
Operative Note.description: A procedure page belonging to an operation: the intraoperative record, phase record or OR summary. Distinguished from the Procedure Note L1 not by name, which is the same, but by the document the page is bound into. Standing alone it is a treatment record and belongs under Procedure Note.

Operative Note.name: Anesthesia Record
Operative Note.description: The anaesthesia record and post-anaesthesia care, including the transfer of care out of theatre.

Operative Note.name: Critical Care Record
Operative Note.description: Intensive care documentation: ICU flow sheets and ventilator management records.

Operative Note.name: Triage Report
Operative Note.description: The triage assessment taken at presentation, carrying acuity and arrival details.

Operative Note.name: Intra-operative Record
Operative Note.description: Intra-operative nursing / OR record: times, staff, positioning, counts.

Operative Note.name: Implant Record
Operative Note.description: Implant log or sticker page: devices, lot numbers.

Operative Note.name: Others
Operative Note.description: An operative page that fits none of the above, such as an implant log.

Procedure Note.name: Dialysis Record
Procedure Note.description: A dialysis run: treatment record, haemodialysis flow sheet or peritoneal dialysis record. Logged per session rather than written up per visit.

Procedure Note.name: Infusion and Chemotherapy
Procedure Note.description: Administration of an infusion or chemotherapy, including the cycle and the agents given.

Procedure Note.name: Radiation Therapy
Procedure Note.description: A radiation therapy treatment record: fields, fractions and dose delivered.

Procedure Note.name: Wound Care
Procedure Note.description: Wound and burn treatment: measurements, debridement and dressing changes, recorded per session.

Procedure Note.name: Therapy Session
Procedure Note.description: A therapy treatment session: physical, occupational, speech, respiratory, cardiac rehabilitation, chiropractic or acupuncture. The therapy DISCHARGE summary is Discharge Summary instead.

Procedure Note.name: Elastography
Procedure Note.description: An elastography or FibroScan procedure measuring tissue stiffness.

Procedure Note.name: Injection Visit
Procedure Note.description: A visit whose purpose is an injection, with the agent and site recorded.

Procedure Note.name: Knee Procedure
Procedure Note.description: A procedure performed on the knee: injection, aspiration or arthrocentesis, written up on its own. The site is the L2 because it is what the code turns on.

Procedure Note.name: Laser Procedure
Procedure Note.description: A laser treatment, including YAG and SLT.

Procedure Note.name: Lumbar Procedure
Procedure Note.description: A procedure performed on the lumbar spine: injection, aspiration or arthrocentesis, written up on its own. The site is the L2 because it is what the code turns on.

Procedure Note.name: Office Procedure
Procedure Note.description: A procedure performed in the office where no more specific type is identified, including gastroenterology and retinal office procedures.

Procedure Note.name: Pathology Procedure
Procedure Note.description: A procedure carried out in the pathology laboratory, such as gross examination.

Procedure Note.name: Endoscopy (EGD)
Procedure Note.description: Endoscopy procedure record (EGD) when kept as a procedure note rather than a report.

Procedure Note.name: Cardiac Procedure
Procedure Note.description: Cardiac procedure record (cardioversion, cath-lab procedure log) that is not a study report.

Procedure Note.name: Others
Procedure Note.description: A treatment record or procedure page with no specific procedure identified. A page headed only 'Procedure Note' with no site or modality lands here, because that is the label an unsure annotator reaches for.

Discharge Summary.name: Depart/Discharge Note
Discharge Summary.description: The discharge summary itself, in any of its names: depart note, depart summary, discharge note, discharge report, final case summary.

Discharge Summary.name: Discharge Instruction
Discharge Summary.description: What the patient was told to do after discharge, including the Spanish-language versions of the same form.

Discharge Summary.name: Discharge Medication
Discharge Summary.description: The medication list as it stands at discharge.

Discharge Summary.name: Transfer of Care
Discharge Summary.description: Handover to another facility or service, including anaesthesia transfer of care.

Discharge Summary.name: Interim Summary
Discharge Summary.description: A summary issued mid-stay rather than at discharge.

Discharge Summary.name: Short Stay Summary
Discharge Summary.description: The discharge document for a short stay or observation episode. Its own header governs even where it embeds a history and physical.

Discharge Summary.name: History and Physical
Discharge Summary.description: Admission H&P of an inpatient, observation or short stay. Office H&Ps are Progress Note.

Discharge Summary.name: Consultation Note
Discharge Summary.description: Inpatient consult. Office consults are Progress Note.

Discharge Summary.name: Others
Discharge Summary.description: A discharge-packet page that fits none of the above.

Clinical Summary.name: Summary of Care (C-CDA)
Clinical Summary.description: CCD, Summary of Care, Transition of Care, C-CDA documents.

Clinical Summary.name: After-Visit Summary
Clinical Summary.description: After Visit Summary / Patient Clinical Summary given at the end of a visit.

Consent and Authorization.name: Consent for Treatment
Consent and Authorization.description: Consent to treatment / conditions of treatment signed by the patient.

Consent and Authorization.name: Assignment of Benefits
Consent and Authorization.description: The patient assigning insurance benefits to the provider.

Consent and Authorization.name: Referral Authorization
Consent and Authorization.description: Approval of a referral, with the visits authorised.

Consent and Authorization.name: Others
Consent and Authorization.description: An administrative page that fits none of the above.

Demographics.name: Patient Information
Demographics.description: The patient's identity, contact and coverage details.

Demographics.name: Face Sheet
Demographics.description: The printed face sheet or registration page. Note that this overlaps Patient Demographics by design: both were asked for, and a face sheet is in practice the demographics page under another name.

Demographics.name: Others
Demographics.description: A demographic page that fits neither of the above.

Immunization.name: Immunization Record
Immunization.description: Vaccines given or due, in any format: immunisation list, vaccination administration record, flu shot record.

Immunization.name: Others
Immunization.description: An immunisation page that fits none of the above.

Medication Record.name: Medication List
Medication Record.description: The current medication list as a standalone page.

Medication Record.name: Blood Transfusion Record
Medication Record.description: Administration of blood or blood products, which is a medication administration rather than a procedure.

Medication Record.name: Others
Medication Record.description: A medication page that fits none of the above.

Order and Requisition.name: Physician Order
Order and Requisition.description: Any order written by a clinician: medication, treatment, service request, post-operative orders.

Order and Requisition.name: Laboratory Requisition
Order and Requisition.description: A requisition or lab form requesting a test.

Order and Requisition.name: Others
Order and Requisition.description: An order or request that fits neither of the above.

Problem List.name: Diagnosis List/Index
Problem List.description: A list or index of diagnoses, often coded, with no assessment.

Forms and Questionnaires.name: Assessment
Forms and Questionnaires.description: A structured assessment or evaluation: functional status, ADL and IADL, nutrition, occupational health, fitness for duty, annual wellness.

Forms and Questionnaires.name: Questionnaire
Forms and Questionnaires.description: A questionnaire, checklist or screening instrument completed about the patient: screening tests, preventive checklists, health maintenance, Mini-Cog and clock drawing, growth charts.

Forms and Questionnaires.name: Others
Forms and Questionnaires.description: A form that is neither clearly a questionnaire nor clearly an assessment.

Provider Letter.name: Referral Letter
Provider Letter.description: Letter referring the patient to another provider.

Provider Letter.name: Consultation Letter
Provider Letter.description: Consultant letter back to the referring provider.

Provider Letter.name: Records Request
Provider Letter.description: Any letter, fax or EHR note whose purpose is requesting records.

Patient Communication.name: Patient Message
Patient Communication.description: A message exchanged with the patient: telephone message, portal communication, web encounter.

Patient Communication.name: Notice
Patient Communication.description: A notice or notification sent to the patient, including discharge notices.

Patient Communication.name: Patient Education Material
Patient Communication.description: Educational material and patient instructions given out as their own document.

Patient Communication.name: Telephone Encounter
Patient Communication.description: Phone note, refill call, telephone message.

Patient Communication.name: Others
Patient Communication.description: A communication page that fits none of the above.

Administrative.name: Appointment Record
Administrative.description: Appointment notes and summaries: when the patient was or is due to be seen.

Administrative.name: Billing & Invoices
Administrative.description: Invoices, billing pages, superbills, charge sheets and estimates. Codeability here can depend on the ingest source rather than the page.

Administrative.name: Patient Registration
Administrative.description: Registration / intake demographics form for registration.

Administrative.name: Superbill
Administrative.description: Encounter form / superbill with ICD-10 and CPT codes. Invoices and statements stay Billing & Invoices.

Administrative.name: Others
Administrative.description: An administrative page that fits none of the above.

specialty.name: Anesthesia
specialty.description: Anaesthesia and peri-anaesthetic care. Evidence: ASA class, induction, intubation, PACU.

specialty.name: Audiology
specialty.description: Hearing and balance, including ENT. Evidence: audiogram, tympanometry, speech discrimination.

specialty.name: Behavioral Health
specialty.description: Psychiatry, psychology and substance use. Evidence: PHQ-9, GAD-7, psychotherapy, mental status.

specialty.name: Cardiology
specialty.description: Heart and vascular. Evidence: echocardiogram, ejection fraction, pacemaker, telemetry.

specialty.name: Critical Care
specialty.description: ICU and intensive care. Evidence: ventilator settings, drips, hourly flow sheet.

specialty.name: Dermatology
specialty.description: Skin. Evidence: Mohs, skin biopsy, lesion, melanoma, cryotherapy.

specialty.name: Dialysis
specialty.description: Renal replacement therapy, separate from general nephrology. Evidence: hemodialysis, peritoneal dialysis, AV fistula.

specialty.name: Emergency
specialty.description: Emergency department, urgent care and prehospital. Evidence: triage, ESI level, ED course, disposition.

specialty.name: Gastroenterology
specialty.description: Digestive tract. Evidence: colonoscopy, EGD, sigmoidoscopy, polyp.

specialty.name: Home Health
specialty.description: Care delivered in the home. Evidence: OASIS, homebound, face-to-face encounter.

specialty.name: Infusion
specialty.description: Infusion therapy as a service line. Evidence: infusion centre, cycle, administration record.

specialty.name: Nephrology
specialty.description: Kidney disease outside dialysis. Evidence: creatinine clearance, ESRD, renal failure.

specialty.name: Neurology
specialty.description: Nervous system. Evidence: EEG, EMG, nerve conduction, seizure, neuropathy.

specialty.name: Nursing
specialty.description: Nursing documentation. Evidence: intake and output, shift assessment, repositioning.

specialty.name: Obstetrics and Gynecology
specialty.description: Pregnancy and women's health. Evidence: prenatal, gestational age, fetal heart, colposcopy.

specialty.name: Occupational Health
specialty.description: Employer-directed and workers' compensation care. Evidence: fitness for duty, work restriction, return to work.

specialty.name: Oncology
specialty.description: Cancer care. Evidence: chemotherapy, staging, metastatic, radiation therapy.

specialty.name: Ophthalmology
specialty.description: Eye care, optometry included. Evidence: OD/OS, IOP, visual acuity, fundus, slit lamp.

specialty.name: Orthopedics
specialty.description: Musculoskeletal and sports medicine. Evidence: arthroplasty, rotator cuff, fracture, range of motion.

specialty.name: Palliative Care
specialty.description: Palliative, hospice and pain management. Evidence: goals of care, comfort measures, pain score, MME.

specialty.name: Pathology
specialty.description: Tissue and cytology. Evidence: specimen, gross description, microscopic, immunohistochemistry.

specialty.name: Primary Care
specialty.description: Family medicine, internal medicine, general practice. Evidence: annual wellness, health maintenance.

specialty.name: Pulmonology
specialty.description: Lungs and respiratory. Evidence: spirometry, PFT, COPD, FEV1.

specialty.name: Radiology
specialty.description: Imaging as a service line. Evidence: imaging centre letterhead, contrast, tomography.

specialty.name: Rehabilitation
specialty.description: Physical, occupational and speech therapy, chiropractic. Evidence: gait training, therapeutic exercise, plan of care units.

specialty.name: Sleep Study
specialty.description: Sleep medicine. Evidence: polysomnography, apnea, CPAP, titration.

specialty.name: Surgery
specialty.description: General and surgical specialties. Evidence: estimated blood loss, specimen removed, wound closure.

specialty.name: Urology
specialty.description: Urinary tract and male reproductive. Evidence: cystoscopy, prostate, PSA, urodynamic.

specialty.name: Wound Care
specialty.description: Wound and burn management. Evidence: wound measurements, debridement, dressing change.

specialty.name: Pain Management
specialty.description: Pain management and interventional pain: injections, nerve blocks, pain clinic notes.

specialty.name: Others
specialty.description: A real service line this list does not yet carry. Annotator only; the detector never emits it, because it cannot recognise what it has no lexicon for. Seeing this value is the signal to add a specialty.

specialty.name: Unknown
specialty.description: No specialty signal on the page at all. This is a correct answer, not a miss: a specialty is detectable on 43% of pages alone and 33% more by inheriting from the document.

rules.section_L1_note: Under Progress Note, L2 is the content section on the page (axis B), decided by section tagging. It is confirmed in the tool and not trained.
rules.specialty_note: 'Unknown' means no signal on the page; 'Others' means a real service line the list does not carry yet, the signal to extend the lexicon.
rules.note_v29_2: Labels follow Training/processed/taxonomy_v29.json context_rules (page_essence etc.). Section L1 (Progress Note) L2 is owned by section tagging at inference, as before.
